findings.title: LeanCTX is simultaneously declared conditional and globally active

observation.actualBehavior: The tool ladder and tool registry make LeanCTX conditional, while the final AGENTS.md block states that LeanCTX is active and replaces native equivalents.
observation.expectedBehavior: One canonical status and invocation rule must be expressed consistently across the execution policy, registry, host adapter and configuration.

evidence.resultSummary: Defines the repository execution entry point, conditional tool ladder, authority separation and a final LeanCTX active block.

rootCause.immediateCause: A host-generated activation block was appended without reconciliation with the canonical conditional-tool model.
rootCause.structuralCause: The adapter activation lifecycle is not generated from or checked against the tool registry.
rootCause.incorrectOrMissingTruthOwner: Governance Contract Authority with Platform Tooling Owner

truthOwnership.correctOwner: Governance Contract Authority with Platform Tooling Owner

resolution.strategy: Choose the intended LeanCTX lifecycle state, encode it once in the canonical registry, generate or validate all projections, and add a contradiction guard.

criteria.statement: AGENTS.md, the tool registry, .agents/tools/leanctx.md and host configuration express one state with one evidence boundary.

findings.title: Platform adapter registration is incomplete and asymmetrical

observation.actualBehavior: Authority precedence classifies Claude, Gemini and LeanCTX adapters, but the agent registry visibly registers only Antigravity and Gemini adapters while other host instructions/configurations exist.
observation.expectedBehavior: Every supported host adapter must either be registered with bounded capabilities or explicitly classified outside the agent registry by a checked rule.

evidence.resultSummary: Defines authority ranks and classifies agents, skills, guards, adapters and derived tool registry.

rootCause.immediateCause: Adapter files were added by host integration paths without one mandatory registry-coverage invariant.
rootCause.structuralCause: The agent registry and authority document classify overlapping but non-identical adapter sets.

resolution.strategy: Define the complete adapter inventory, register each supported adapter or explicitly exclude it, and validate one-to-one coverage.

criteria.statement: All live host adapters have a machine-readable lifecycle, owner, capability boundary and primary file.

findings.title: Tool truth is split across an AI registry and a broad operational catalog

observation.actualBehavior: The governance agent-tool registry contains three conditional AI tools, while a separate v5 catalog owns broad tool IDs, activation, decisions and failure policies across several files.
observation.expectedBehavior: One declared canonical tool model must own identity, lifecycle, activation, owner and evidence boundary, with narrower registries generated or explicitly scoped projections.

evidence.resultSummary: Defines authority ranks and classifies agents, skills, guards, adapters and derived tool registry.

rootCause.immediateCause: The AI-agent tool model and the operational OSS toolchain evolved independently.
rootCause.structuralCause: Authority precedence classifies the agent-tool registry as derived support but does not clearly name the canonical owner of the broad operational catalog.
rootCause.incorrectOrMissingTruthOwner: Governance Contract Authority and Platform Tooling Owner

truthOwnership.correctOwner: Governance Contract Authority and Platform Tooling Owner

resolution.strategy: Select a canonical tool schema and owner, merge shared lifecycle fields, and generate scoped projections for agent routing and operational activation.

criteria.statement: No tool ID or activation state has two writable owners; all projections are reproducible and drift-checked.

findings.title: Registered agent and tool guards are not unified in the default diagnosis or observed CI policy path

observation.actualBehavior: The registry and package scripts define document-authority, same-commit, tool-catalog, toolchain-activation and OSS-toolchain guards, but guard:governance-all and the inspected CI policy/diagnostics workflows do not visibly execute the complete set.
observation.expectedBehavior: A single fail-closed agent-system aggregate must cover every mandatory registered invariant locally and in CI when relevant paths change.

evidence.resultSummary: Registers governance, agent, authority, toolchain, workflow and repository guards.

rootCause.immediateCause: New guards were registered and exposed individually without being added to one authoritative aggregate and workflow route.
rootCause.structuralCause: Registration, local aggregation and CI routing are separately maintained surfaces.
rootCause.incorrectOrMissingTruthOwner: CI Workflow Authority and Governance Contract Authority

truthOwnership.correctOwner: CI Workflow Authority and Governance Contract Authority

resolution.strategy: Create one manifest-driven agent-system aggregate, route it from local diagnose and CI, and make the guard-registry gate prove mandatory reachability.

criteria.statement: Every mandatory guard has one package command and one applicable CI path; no registered mandatory guard is dormant.

findings.title: The pinned branch head has no current CI status or workflow-run evidence
